title: The context window
summary: Claude's working memory is a desk of fixed size. Everything it reads takes room, old papers get boiled down to a summary, and a new session starts with a clear desk.
note: Names, companies and files here are **made-up examples**.

props.title: A desk of fixed size
props.body: Everything Claude is working with has to fit on it. **Where it stops:** a desk holds paper; this holds text, counted in **tokens**, chunks of about 3½ characters of English.

props.text: Why did Acme's orders drop in March?

props.title: Compaction
props.md:
**Kept:** a summary: your requests, key snippets, pending tasks and current work.

**Lost:** the exact text of old outputs, and possibly details of early instructions.

**Re-read in full:** the project's CLAUDE.md, from disk.

items.label: Claude Code's own instructions and tools

props.title: Look at your own desk
props.expect: In Claude Code, type `/context` and press Return. It draws your context window as a grid of coloured squares, broken down by what is using the room, with tips on what to trim.

steps.title: A desk of fixed size
steps.text: Claude's working memory is its **context window**: everything it can see at once, with a fixed size. Think of a desk. Even before you type, a little is taken by Claude Code's own instructions and its list of tools.

steps.title: CLAUDE.md goes on first
steps.text: If your project has a **CLAUDE.md** file, its standing instructions are laid on the desk at the start of every session, before your first message.

items.label: Claude Code's own instructions and tools

steps.title: Everything it reads
steps.text: Your message goes on the desk, then every file Claude reads and every reply it writes. Each one takes room.

items.label: Claude Code's own instructions and tools

steps.title: Big printouts crowd it
steps.text: Keep working and the desk fills. Long outputs take the most room: a whole log, a whole spreadsheet. Claude Code caps a single command's output (past about 30,000 characters, Claude gets a preview and the rest is saved to a file), but outputs add up fast.

items.label: Claude Code's own instructions and tools

steps.title: Old papers get boiled down
steps.text: As the desk nears full, Claude Code makes room by itself. It clears old outputs first, then boils the conversation down to a summary: **compaction**. Your project's CLAUDE.md is read again from disk, so it survives in full.

items.label: Claude Code's own instructions and tools

steps.title: A new session: a clear desk
steps.text: Start a new session, or type `/clear`, and the desk is cleared. Nothing from the last conversation comes along unless it was written down. Only the standing papers are laid out again: Claude Code's own instructions, your CLAUDE.md and a few other start-up items.

steps.title: The whole picture
steps.text: These numbers are illustrative. A real desk's size depends on the model, from 200,000 to 1 million tokens. Keep CLAUDE.md short, and keep big outputs off the desk: the next explainer shows how.
